steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test, treated vs control

steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control human heart samples at FDR 0.05, with control as the reference level?

grounding.reason: Raw counts, fixed-effects two-group design at 6 replicates per group: DESeq2 Wald with apeglm shrinkage (R-0001, R-0009), minimal pre-filter plus independent filtering (R-0029, R-0002), size factors inside the model (R-0026, R-0030), explicit reference level and named contrast (R-0036), BH at alpha 0.05 with the p-value histogram inspected (R-0010, R-0083, R-0043). Keep independent filtering on and set alpha = 0.05 in results()
Use apeglm via lfcShrink on the coefficient, and keep the unshrunken estimate in the table

steps.description: Fit the differential expression model on the raw counts from counts.csv with the sample table from metadata.csv. Pre-filter minimally: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size). Set the condition factor with control as the explicit reference level — do not rely on alphabetical ordering. Design ~condition. Run the Wald test and extract results with contrast = c('condition','treated','control') so a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated. Keep independent filtering on and pass alpha = 0.05 to results(). Plot the histogram of unadjusted p-values before reading the adjusted values and describe its shape. plan.title: Heart total-RNA treated vs control DE + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single 12,000 x 12 gene-level Salmon count matrix (counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column) with a 12 x 2 sample table (metadata.csv) giving one condition column: 6 treated vs 6 control human heart samples, unpaired, one batch. The question is purely 'which genes differ between treated and control', so the backbone is a two-group negative-binomial test with an enrichment pass for interpretation.

Two data caveats shape the QC step rather than the model. (1) Duplication rate above 60 percent in most libraries: these are rRNA-depleted total-RNA libraries WITHOUT UMIs, so duplicates must NOT be removed — in RNA-seq the duplication rate tracks expression level, and de-duplication without UMIs deletes real signal. The duplication rate is reported per sample beside library size and detected genes, and is only actionable if one library combines an outlying duplication rate with low complexity. (2) sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median. It is kept through QC and inspected on the PCA and the sample-distance heatmap; DESeq2's median-of-ratios size factor already accounts for depth, so depth alone is not grounds for exclusion. Removal, if any, must be justified in writing from the QC plots, and the DE step must then be reported both with and without it.

Because the libraries are rRNA-depleted total RNA, the QC step also reports the residual rRNA/mitochondrial share and a proxy for non-coding/pre-mRNA content computable from a gene-level matrix (MT- gene share, RNA45S/RNA5-8S/RNA18S/RNA28S and RN7SK/RN7SL/MALAT1/NEAT1 share). Where a metric needs read-level information the matrix does not carry (true intronic fraction), the step must say so rather than approximate it silently.

Modelling: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios normalization inside the model, design ~condition with control set explicitly as the reference level, contrast (condition, treated, control), Wald test, apeglm shrinkage for reporting/ranking, BH with independent filtering at alpha 0.05. With 6 per group DESeq2 flags count outliers by Cook's distance and returns NA p-values rather than replacing counts; those genes are counted and reported separately from the genes the independent filter removed. edgeR quasi-likelihood runs on the same counts and design as a second method; the intersection is the high-confidence set and the union is never reported as the result.

Interpretation: preranked fgsea on the DESeq2 Wald statistic (chosen over signed p-value, which ties at saturation, and over the unshrunken LFC, which is noisy at low counts) against human MSigDB Hallmark first, then Reactome and human WikiPathways as separate collections with separate FDR — never merged. With only ~12,000 genes in the matrix, some gene sets will be under-represented, so the tested-gene universe and per-collection set counts after the 15-500 size window must be reported. A discrete over-representation test is only run if more than 50 genes pass FDR 0.05.

Note on tximport: the profile states the counts are already summarized to gene level in a CSV, so the transcript-level abundance and length matrices needed for a tximport length offset are not available. The DE step must state this and proceed on the count matrix without length offsets, flagging that a gene whose isoform usage shifts can be miscalled.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library size and detected genes per sample
Low count filter: at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples
~ condition with control as explicit reference level; contrast condition treated vs control
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering, alpha 0.05, p-value histogram inspected
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as robustness second method
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic, Hallmark then Reactome and WikiPathways
Reproducible report: MA plot, dispersion plot, effect columns, leading edge, sessionInfo

steps.question: Which treated-vs-control genes are called by both DESeq2 Wald and edgeR quasi-likelihood, and which are called by only one?
steps.description: Run edgeR on the same counts.csv matrix, the same sample set, the same pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples) and the same design ~condition with control as reference. Use TMM normalization factors, estimate dispersions with estimateDisp, fit glmQLFit and test the treated-vs-control coefficient with glmQLFTest. Adjust with BH and call genes at FDR 0.05. Then compare against the DESeq2 result from T1S2: report the number of significant genes from each method, the size of the intersection, and the genes unique to each method labelled with the method that called them. Present the intersection as the high-confidence set. Do not report the union as the result. Cross-tabulate the direction of the log fold change between the two methods for the intersection genes.
steps.context: Robustness check at the low end of the replicate range. Both tools control FDR at 6 replicates per group but disagree on some genes, and the disagreement concentrates at low counts.
acceptance_criteria: An edgeR results table for the same tested genes with logFC, F, PValue and FDR
A comparison table: n significant by DESeq2, n significant by edgeR, n in the intersection, n unique to each
The intersection is explicitly labelled the high-confidence set and the union is not presented as the result
Fold-change direction agreement across the intersection is reported
constraints: Use exactly the same pre-filter, sample set and design as T1S2
Use TMM normalization factors inside the edgeR model; do not pre-normalize the counts
Use the quasi-likelihood F-test (glmQLFit + glmQLFTest), not the likelihood ratio test
Call significance by FDR at 0.05, matching T1S2
caveats: Disagreement between the two methods grows at low counts and at low replicate numbers; a method-unique gene is weaker evidence, not a finding of one method being wrong

grounding.reason: edgeR quasi-likelihood is the permitted second method at 2-11 replicates per group (R-0001), and R-0042 requires reporting both counts and their intersection as the high-confidence set rather than the union.

steps.name: Preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic
steps.question: Which pathways are coordinately up or down in treated versus control heart, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic?
steps.description: Take the full DESeq2 results table from T1S2 — every tested gene, not a thresholded subset — and rank genes by the Wald statistic (the stat column). State this choice explicitly in the output: the Wald statistic is signed and scaled by its standard error, unlike the unshrunken log2 fold change, which is noisy for low-count genes, and unlike a signed p-value, which ties when p-values saturate. Run fgsea against three human gene set collections independently, each with its own BH adjustment and its own release stated: (1) the MSigDB human hallmark collection, (2) the Reactome pathway collection filtered to Homo sapiens using the accompanying pathway index, (3) the human WikiPathways collection, splitting the '%'-delimited descriptor to recover readable set names. Apply a 15-500 gene size window AFTER intersecting each set with the tested genes, and report the number of sets that survive per collection. Do not merge the three collections into one set list. Collapse redundant significant sets by leading-edge overlap and report one representative per group with the full table kept as a supplement. Report the leading-edge genes of each significant set together with their Wald statistic, and mark leading-edge overlap between reported sets. The identifiers in counts.csv are gene symbols and all three collections are symbol-based, so no Entrez mapping is required; report the share of tested genes that appear in no set of each collection. Only if more than 50 genes pass padj < 0.05 in T1S2, additionally run an over-representation test on that discrete list with the tested genes as the universe; otherwise state the size of the significant list and skip ORA. Set and record a random seed for the fgsea permutations.
steps.context: Human heart, treated vs control. Reference data needed: human hallmark gene sets, a Reactome pathway GMT with a species index to restrict to Homo sapiens, and a human WikiPathways GMT — all symbol-based. Resolve each against what the environment holds at run time and report the release of each; if one collection is absent, run the remaining collections and report the gap rather than substituting another organism's sets.
acceptance_criteria: Three separate fgsea result tables, one per collection, each with pathway, NES, pval, padj, size and leading edge
The ranking metric (Wald stat) is stated with the reason it was chosen over the alternatives
The release/version of each gene set collection is named beside its results
Number of sets tested per collection after intersecting with the tested genes and applying the 15-500 window is reported
Leading-edge genes with their Wald statistics are listed for each significant set, with overlap between reported sets marked
Redundant significant sets are collapsed to representatives, with the full table retained
The random seed is recorded
constraints: Rank the FULL list of tested genes; never cut the list at padj or fold change before fgsea
Apply the 15-500 size window after intersecting each set with the tested genes
Use the human collections only — never the mouse or rat WikiPathways file
Filter the Reactome GMT to Homo sapiens via the pathway index before testing
Do not merge collections; adjust p-values within each collection separately
Only run an over-representation test if more than 50 genes pass padj < 0.05, and then use the tested genes as the universe, never the whole genome
State the release of each collection in the output
caveats: The matrix carries ~12,000 genes, so many sets will lose members to the intersection; a small tested-set count weakens any single hit
Gene length and expression level bias which genes reach significance; this is why the ranked test on all tested genes is preferred to a list-based test
Enrichment results are method-dependent — a set is a hypothesis for follow-up, not a demonstrated mechanism

grounding.reason: Preranked fgsea on the full tested list is the default enrichment after a DE test (R-0107, R-0045); for the disputed ranking metric (R-0108) this plan chooses the DESeq2 Wald statistic per R-0099; Hallmark first then Reactome and WikiPathways as separate collections with releases stated (R-0048, R-0098, R-0165); 15-500 window on the intersected sets and the tested-gene universe (R-0047, R-0046, R-0054); ORA suppressed below 50 significant genes (R-0103). Identifiers are already symbols matching the symbol GMTs, so no Entrez remap is needed (R-0101).

steps.name: Consolidated report
steps.question: What is the reproducible, fully-caveated answer to 'which genes differ between treated and control' in this 6-vs-6 human heart total-RNA dataset?
steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S1, T1S2, T1S3 and T2S1. Before any gene table, state: the method and version of each package, the design formula ~condition, the reference level (control) and the contrast (condition, treated, control), the padj threshold and any fold-change threshold, the number of genes tested after the pre-filter, and the number of differentially expressed genes. Include the two fit diagnostics — the MA plot with significant genes marked, and the dispersion plot showing the per-gene estimates, the fitted trend and the shrunken values — and say what each shows. Give the gene table with baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, stat, pvalue and padj, ranked by the shrunken log2 fold change, with the shrinkage estimator named in the header. Carry through the DESeq2/edgeR overlap from T1S3 with the intersection identified as the high-confidence set. Carry through the enrichment results from T2S1 with the collection releases, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window and the leading-edge genes, and state that enrichment results depend on the method chosen. Report the QC facts prominently: the duplication rate per sample with the statement that duplicates were not removed and why, and sample_01's library size with the decision taken about it. Attach a reproducibility record: sessionInfo, every package version, the random seed used for the fgsea permutations, and the version of each gene set collection.
steps.context: Consolidation only; no new statistics are fitted here.
acceptance_criteria: Method, package versions, design formula, reference level, contrast, thresholds, number tested and number DE all appear before the gene tables
MA plot and dispersion plot are included with an explanation of each
Gene table carries both the unshrunken and shrunken log2 fold change plus lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value, with apeglm named
DESeq2 vs edgeR overlap is reported with the intersection labelled high-confidence
Enrichment section states the collection, its release, the ranking metric, the universe and the size window, and lists leading-edge genes
Duplication rate and the no-de-duplication decision, and sample_01's depth and the decision taken, are both stated
A reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions, seed and collection versions is attached to the results
constraints: Rank the gene table by the shrunken log2 fold change, never by the unshrunken value alone
Keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit — shrinkage does not change the test
Do not present the union of the DESeq2 and edgeR gene sets as the result
State the enrichment method-dependence caveat explicitly
Do not overstate: with 6 per group and ~12,000 genes, report effect sizes and uncertainty rather than mechanism claims
caveats: A pathway hit is a hypothesis for follow-up, not a demonstrated mechanism
If sample_01 was excluded, every headline number must say whether it comes from the 12-sample or the 11-sample analysis

grounding.reason: Report contents follow the returned report step: method, versions, design, thresholds and counts before the tables (R-0041), both LFC columns with the shrunken value used for ranking (R-0085), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087), two-method overlap (R-0042), enrichment provenance and method-dependence (R-0051, R-0055), leading edge per set (R-0105), and a reproducibility record (R-0086).
